Motivation isn't a plan. "If X happens, then I'll do Y" is.

Psychologists call these implementation intentions, and they're one of the best-supported tools for building habits.

Comment your if-then plan below 👇

#habits #productivity #atomichabits #selfdiscipline #microlearning #psychology #goals #dailyhabits

Rome couldn't beat Hannibal in battle, so Fabius Maximus stopped giving him battles.

They called him "the Delayer" as an insult. History remembers it as strategy.

Where in your life are you fighting on someone else's terms?

#history #strategy #ancientrome #stoicism #leadership #microlearning #historyfacts #mindset

In 1932, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight emus. The emus won.

The lesson isn't about birds. Raw force fails against a scattered problem.

Tag someone who's fighting emus at work right now 🪶

#history #historyfacts #emuwar #strategy #funnyhistory #microlearning #problemsolving #didyouknow

That embarrassing thing you did? Far fewer people noticed than you think.

Psychologists call it the spotlight effect: we overestimate how much others notice us, because everyone is busy thinking about themselves.

Send this to a friend who's still cringing about last week.

#psychology #spotlighteffect #socialanxiety #mindset #confidence #microlearning #psychologyfacts #selfimprovement

A tomato-shaped kitchen timer became one of the world's best-known focus methods.

25 minutes on one task. 5 minutes off. Repeat.

Try one round today and comment 🍅 when it rings.

#pomodoro #productivity #focus #studytips #deepwork #timemanagement #microlearning #habits

Hanoi, 1902: pay people per rat tail, get more rats.

Reward a number and people will deliver the number, not the result you wanted.

Where have you seen a target backfire?

#history #cobraeffect #incentives #economics #strategy #historyfacts #microlearning #leadership

You love the wobbly shelf because you built it.

The IKEA effect: effort makes us overvalue our own creations. Great for furniture, risky for bad ideas.

What's your wobbly shelf?

#psychology #ikeaeffect #behavioraleconomics #cognitivebias #mindset #microlearning #psychologyfacts #decisionmaking

If it takes less than two minutes, do it now.

David Allen's rule from Getting Things Done clears the tiny tasks that clog your list and your head.

Do one two-minute task right after this video.

#productivity #gtd #twominuterule #timemanagement #habits #getthingsdone #microlearning #todolist

The bullet holes that mattered were the ones nobody could see.

Survivorship bias: we study the winners and forget everyone who didn't make it back.

Next time you read a success story, ask who's missing.

#survivorshipbias #history #ww2history #criticalthinking #strategy #cognitivebias #microlearning #statistics

Walked into a room and forgot why? Blame the door.

Research suggests doorways act as event boundaries: your brain files away the last scene, and your mission with it.

Fix: say it out loud before you move.

#psychology #memory #doorwayeffect #brainfacts #neuroscience #microlearning #psychologyfacts #mindset

Work expands to fill the time you give it.

Parkinson's Law, 1955. The fix: set a shorter deadline before you start.

What task are you giving too much time?

#parkinsonslaw #productivity #timemanagement #deadlines #focus #habits #microlearning #worksmarter

Stuck on a problem? Explain it out loud to a rubber duck.

Programmers swear by it. Putting a problem into plain words forces you to find the gap in your own thinking.

The duck is always right 🦆

#rubberduckdebugging #problemsolving #productivity #programming #thinking #microlearning #learning #mindset
